description: Complete-backup retention configuration. Single source of truth mirrored by convex/operations/backups/slot.ts; tests/i5 asserts the two cannot drift. Frequent complete sets are kept 48 hours; daily complete sets (the first slot of each UTC day) are kept through day 14. Media objects are pooled and shared across sets: collection is reference-aware and deletes an object only when NO surviving manifest references it. Deleted-source content cannot survive backups beyond 30 days: the retention invariant (no set outlives 14 days) holds by construction and is asserted at runtime and in tests, so a future retention extension that would break the 30-day bound fails loudly instead of silently keeping purged bytes.

schedule.note: Daily (02:00 UTC) during the pre-user phase: explicit owner decision of 2026-09-25 recorded in docs/adr/mvp-cost-envelope-2026-09.md. The accepted alpha cadence of 15 minutes returns with the first users by the same kind of explicit decision. Frequency is never changed silently to fit a plan. The cadence is owned in TWO places that tests keep equal: this file and the backup Container's cron trigger (apps/backup-worker/wrangler.jsonc).

daily.window: through day 14 (selection: the first slot of each UTC day; with the daily cadence every slot)

deletedContent.enforcement: purged-source media is excluded from NEW sets at build time; every set expires within 14 days, so backup content cannot outlive 30 days; the invariant retention <= 30d is asserted at runtime (beginRun refuses on violation) and in tests/i5

freshness.measuredFrom: database snapshot time (snapshotAtMs of the newest VERIFIED manifest), never completion time
freshness.alerting: ops.backup.stale diagnostic (deduped per episode) past one cadence plus two hours of slack, and backup.job heartbeats every attempt (silence detection fires at three missed cadences)

orphanCollection.note: interrupted runs' pool objects (never referenced by any manifest) are collected after a 48h grace window
